texts: feedback on a story i am writing word count 4983 hello i am new to this subreddit ive been cooking up a story idea for about a year now and have finally decided to make it a reality im making more specifically a comic but i want some help with the story currently i have the main outline but i want some critiques on it ive never put my work out anywhere online before so im a bit nervous but you know i guess i need to get used to this aha note that this is more notes on how to tackle the story for me but again i just want to know if its actually a good story heres a background of the world this is set in in 2027 world war breaks out for a third time and its effects are devastating it lasts for around 5 years before ending with an event that kills three quarters of the world population the event was like a nuclear strike on steroids the story takes place in 2035 3 years after the war has ended the war caused earths climate to become practically unliveable and so a program was launched by a company that specialises in space travel three trained professionals a pilot a scientist and a mechanic are selected to be sent into space to explore and determine whether certain planets are either habitable or can help with restoring earths climate using resources a year into the program however things are paused when the mechanic of the mission goes missing and cannot be found a replacement is put on board our main character and our story begins there act one the story opens with a past recorded video of oliver the scientist ivan the missing mechanic and ana the pilot celebrating ivans birthday aboard the spaceship the footage is warm and playful but ends on an unsettling note when ivans smile falters as he looks past the camera held by ana before the recording abruptly cuts this moment plants early unease and foreshadows later revelations the scene transitions to emily in the present visually mirroring ivans physical position as she eats a meal at a table in a home setting emilys daily life is marked by emotional distance and quiet suffocation at home she is physically present but disengaged surrounded by her mother and younger brother yet unable to connect meaningfully with them news reports about worsening climate conditions play in the background largely ignored her mothers interactions with her are transactional focused on responsibility rather than conversation reinforcing emilys sense of being trapped after an argument breaks out with emilys brother and her mother her mother asks emily to walk her brother to school emily takes her brother to school and then commutes to work passing a protest outside a store selling oxygen masks a necessity in todays society due to the worsening climate during the confrontation she overhears people discussing ivan credited as one of the minds behind the technology whom emily believes is still part of the space mission the protestors openly criticize the company responsible for the program doing space travel as ivan is directly associated with them saying that its taking too long and such emily walks away only for it to be revealed that she herself works for that same company at work emily is shown to be highly capable and quietly indispensable she manufactures requested machinery fixes equipment for coworkers and operates under poor conditions without complaint when a serious accident nearly kills a colleague due to faulty wiring emily intervenes and saves them using her expertise despite being praised she reacts with visible distress brushing off attention rather than accepting it immediately after emily is summoned by her boss and informed of a hiccup in the space program a crewmate is missing and the company is desperate for a replacement emily is asked to be said replacement while they try to find ivan the request is framed less as an honor and more as a necessity it is also revealed here that emily applied for this job a year ago but got rejected in favour of ivan after being deemed mentally unstable after a work incident however is being picked now since she is the only one qualified enough for the position after brief hesitation she agrees that evening emily informs her family her mother and brother react poorly leading to an argument her mother doesnt want her to leave since emily is the main source of income for the family but also the main caretaker emily who does really want the job for her own selfish desires pursues the job regardless while she does feel a sense of responsibility for her family she wants to also take this job seeing it as an escape out of both her family life and earths horrible climate after a short time skip emily travels to the united states for the programs launch though her relationship with her mother remains unresolved she is given a tour of the facility and the spaceship itself she meets oliver who immediately attempts to put her at ease they get along though his enthusiasm contrasts with her restraint notably she does not yet meet ana that evening she attends a public relations event announcing the programs continuation following ivans disappearance emily is uneasy but supported by olivers presence ana and the programs director are present but not formally introduced emily delivers a speech that is awkward yet sincere managing to hold her ground despite visible protests afterward she retreats to a hallway to calm herself and briefly encounters a woman who makes an offhand comment about her new position asking her if its what she really wants the interaction is brief but its directness leaves emily confused on launch day emily is formally introduced to the crewoliver the director and ana who is revealed to be the same woman from the hallway emily is immediately uncomfortable but unable to withdraw before boarding she checks her phone and receives a short but reassuring message from her mother showing that while things are still unresolved between them there is still care act one ends with emily boarding the spaceship uncertain displaced but determined act two takes place several weeks after launch the act opens aboard the spaceship with emily repairing a malfunction in the cockpit ana observes closely marking items off a checklist as emily explains the problem and her solution oliver enters midtask having a cheery demeanour before mentioning that they are approaching their first target planet before landing ana briefs the crew on the planet and stresses strict adherence to protocol emily has no issue following orders but is still weary around ana while oliver appears uneasy with anas tone upon arrival they discover the planet is a barren wasteland contradicting the data ana was given evidence of a massive asteroid impact suggests a longpast mass extinction oliver questions the value of staying noting there is nothing viable for him to sample ana hesitates torn between mission expectations and the evidence in front of her without permission emily ventures ahead and discovers a network of underground caves although this leads the team to continue the mission ana grows noticeably colder toward emily for defying her authority as they explore emily proves her skill modifying equipment on the fly however she slips up at moments as well too eager to explore areas that ana has to prevent her from going to since they are dangerous despite this oliver becomes increasingly impressed and engages more openly with emily while anas frustration mounts after 3 days of searching with no tangible results ana orders a withdrawal emily argues to continue believing she is close to something meaningful but ultimately concedes that anas reasoning is sound they havent found a thing they return to the ship and set course for a second planet in the same system the first planets trip is rather short in comparison to the rest of the storys events later oliver reassures emily that her work mattered and admits that under different circumstances they might have found something significant during this conversation he reveals that ana is the directors daughter that night while on watch duty emily reviews mission logs from the first planet unsettled by a lingering feeling that something was missed while reorganizing nearby equipment she discovers old photographs and recordings of ivan oliver and ana after hesitating she watches one of the tapes a seemingly harmless moment between the three ana enters midviewing and reacts with disproportionate anger emily apologizes which calms ana down but its obvious that the mention of ivan struck a nerve for her emily awkwardly goes back to her station the next day the crew then arrives at the second planet which contrasts sharply with the firstlush vibrant and teeming with plant life the planet is marked uninhabitable due to a weak atmosphere despite its abundance of plants they determine the flora would not survive earths conditions due to how it can only survive in extremities ana is more irritable than before distancing herself from both emily and oliver oliver increasingly anxious stays close to emily and the two talk as they explore oliver shares fragments of his past during the war though he avoids emotional depth his past hints at his tendency of avoidance as his silence caused the deaths of many around him during the war including his family he was basically blackmailed into keeping quiet about government secrets but when he tried to tell people about it his family was killed so hes learnt that silence is survival they soon discover an abandoned human research base ana recognizes it but offers no explanation oliver tells emily that the planet had been studied during the war before being abandoned and that theyre back here to see if there were any unused research or samples that can be used but he doesnt elaborate further inside the base they uncover data suggesting that a rare plant species on one of the planets moons couldat least in theoryaid in restoring earths ecosystems for the first time the team shares a sense of genuine hope and agrees to investigate on the moon they find only a small patch of the plant growing in an extremely hazardous area emily proposes a plan that would safely retrieve the sample but at the cost of valuable resources ana rejects it in favor of a faster riskier approach the argument escalates and emily confronts ana personally bringing up ivan and questioning her judgment oliver remains silent shocked by emilys defiance ana now angered at emilys personal attack proceeds with her plan regardless however midway through it begins to fail causing emily to break away and execute her own plan despite oliver and ana shouting for her to stop fully aware she may die emily presses on framing the risk as both a chance to atone for her past elaborated later and to help save earth she nearly falls to her death but at the last moment ana intervenes pulling her to safety ana is visibly shaken her controlled exterior briefly cracking she says nothing the retrieved sample is damaged but oliver confirms it may still be salvageable with time the act ends with the crew returning to the ship in silence emily watches ana closely beginning to question whether her initial judgment of her was wrong meanwhile the room that emily found the tapes in has a light flashing next to one of the crewmates names a distress signal from ivan which has been going on for months act three opens with a flashback a young girl stands in a hospital corridor with her father doctors speak quietly to him while the girl stares through a window at a room where a woman lies motionless beneath a sheet her expression is eerily blank the father his face never shown explains that the woman is dead that she was the girls mother the child does not respond on the drive home the father tells her gently but firmly that they cannot dwell on this that they must move on and not talk about it again his voice betrays his grief even as he avoids it the girl remains silent only the slightest welling of her eyes suggests feeling beneath the surface the audience does not yet know who she is the story cuts back to the present aboard the ship several days have passed oliver and ana examine the salvaged plant sample but oliver has made little progress and is growing frustrated a restrained argument breaks out between them touching on unresolved tensions from their shared past before emily enters when she asks about the sample oliver dismisses her concern emily instead raises a practical issue one of the ships engines requires maintenance that will take several days and would be safer to complete on a planet ana considers their options and proposes a detour to a nearby planet she and oliver have visited beforestable resourcerich and suitable for both repairs and olivers research suggesting that resources there could even help with the sample emily hesitates about deviating from the plan but ana waves it off surprising her with a rare flexibility emily softens further toward ana while oliver is visibly relieved by the lack of conflict they land on the planet which is strikingly earthlike the atmosphere is breathable the landscape lush and calm emily asks why this planet was never seriously considered as a solution for earth ana explains that the planets seasons last for years with winters and summers so extreme they are lethal they have arrived during a brief deceptive autumn before winter sets in over the following days emily focuses on repairing the ship ana has to give her access control of the ship this is important while ana and oliver gather resources for the sample during downtime emily and oliver explore the planet together laughing and enjoying its beauty ana watches from a distance still reserved but no as cold she treats emily less like a subordinate and more like a teammate during one outing ana discovers something she missed on previous visits and becomes convinced there may be microbial life beyond plant matter emily volunteers to accompany her partly out of curiosity and partly because she is growing increasingly fascinated by ana herself as they search their conversation begins professionally but when emily thanks ana for saving her life weeks earlier something shifts ana initially deflects keeping it formal but eventually opens up as they walk the two exchange fragments of their pasts ana speaks about her strained relationship with her father shaped by emotional distance and unspoken loss this hints that anas desire involves a theme of denial about her situation emily in turn shares her experiences with workplace trauma and her complicated relationship with her mother revealing that during the war she left a coworker to die during an attack on their base this hints at emilys martyr complex how she pushes to help others so much because she feels immense guilt for leaving her coworker behind neither fully unpack their pain but there is recognition and understanding between them it is during this quiet bond that the audience realizes the girl in the opening flashback was ana they discover evidence of lifebacterial not sentientbut still significant the moment feels hopeful with ana collecting samples of the bacteria and saying its worth studying they return to the ship changed more aligned than before while ana and emily were exploring oliver briefly noticed something troubling in the ships systems a faint distress signal bearing ivans identifier he expertly disables the signal implying hes done it before but it doesnt shut off turning from orange to red panicked he covers it over with a blanket and leaves it saying nothing back together the crews dynamic is noticeably warmer ana is less rigid even allowing moments of familiarity with oliver oliver announces progress on the sample and the three share a rare moment of celebration emily feels genuinely fulfilled for the first time she feels she belongs as they resume course to the next planet oliver continues testing one day emily enters the same storage room oliver was in to log planetary data as she prepares to leave she hears a soft irregular blinking curious she removes a covering from a dormant console and finds ivans distress signal still active shaken emily immediately brings ana and oliver to the room she explains that the signal is real and appears to be coming from a nearby planet she insists they investigate and bring ivan back ana shuts it down instantly claiming its a malfunction and turning the signal off when emily presses further ana deflects and urges oliver to back her up his hesitation only deepens emilys suspicion the tension escalates into a heated argument emily accuses them of avoiding the truth under pressure oliver lets something slip just enough to make everyone pause ana freezes emily realises the horrifying implication ivan didnt disappear he was left behind on purpose ana snaps ordering emily to drop it instead emily uses her control of the ship i told you it was important to lock ana and oliver out of the ships navigation and control systems isolating command access she refuses to restore control until they tell her the full truth forced into a corner ana and oliver explain their version of events they describe ivan as unstable obsessed with studying a dangerous alien species on a planet they previously visited unwilling to abandon his research even when ordered they admit they left him there intentionally ana frames it as a necessary decision portraying ivan as recklesspossibly delusional fragmented flashbacks accompany their explanation emily is devastated the betrayal cuts deepest with ana after their seemingly heart to heart she demands they go back for ivan ana refuses outright when emily declares she will go alone ana physically blocks her the argument turns violent the two fight through the ship colliding with equipment and causing damage oliver attempts to intervene but is injured in the chaos emily breaks free and reaches an evacuation pod ana pounds on the door first appealing to logic then to emotion growing increasingly desperate and manipulative emily realizes too late that the pod requires external authorization to launch outside oliver stands at the control his hand near the button that launches the pod ana begs him not to press it emily silently pleads from behind the glass after a long unbearable moment oliver presses the button he chooses this out of his own agency not panic the pod launches emily does not restore control to the ship ana and oliver are left stranded powerless as emily disappears into space the remainder of the act follows emily alone she pilots the pod toward ivans last known location arriving nearly out of rations the planet is eerie almost horror like as she explores grotesque figures emerge creatures that resemble dead humans terrified emily runs panics and falls alone hurt and starving she spirals into regret convinced ana was right and that this was a mistake then she collides with someone emily looks up standing over her is ivanalive battered feral with fear act three ends act four opens in the immediate aftermath of emilys escape on the spaceship there is no explosion of anger only silence ana leans against the glass wall where the evacuation pod once was oliver stands frozen near the launch button for a long moment neither speaks oliver finally tries to say something but ana cuts him off quietly why did you do that her voice is fragile almost broken oliver cant answer she asks again when he still says nothing ana crosses the space between them grabs him by the collar and the tension finally breaks they argue violently not just about emily but about years of unspoken guilt shared responsibility and choices neither of them fully owned all relating to leaving ivan on the planet both end up crying panicked by the realization that they no longer have full control of the ship the argument ends unresolved with ana storming out and oliver left alone in the cockpit the story cuts to the planet emily encounters ivan who thinks shes attacking him and starts attacking her out of self defence she manages to calm him down just long enough to explain who she is but before anything meaningful can be said emily collapses from exhaustion and hunger while unconscious she drifts through fragmented dreams tied to her past traumas her coworker and stuff with her parents when she wakes she finds herself in ivans crude hideout ivan is physically present but emotionally distant muttering to himself studying the evacuation pod blueprint emily carried asking technical questions but refusing to explain anything about how he ended up here she notices that his fingers are blue and one of his eyes are black he is clearly unstable emily begins to doubt herself wondering if ana was right about him after all hoping to gain leverage or understanding emily leaves to search for the evacuation pod that ivan is interested in while doing so she stumbles across a large abandoned structure and realizes with shock that this planet was also studied by humans confused and unsettled she enters the building inside she encounters the planets aliens discovering they are sentient and communicate with one another in a language eerily similar to human speech fragments of russian chinese and english blended together she hides trying to escape unnoticed but eventually finds herself in a room filled with old human equipment and recorded tapes the creatures discover her this time they dont immediately attack one of them visibly less deteriorated than the others speaks to her in english emily is stunned as they speak with emily asking the alien questions another creature enters the room far more decayed and suddenly becomes violent attacking emily emily flees into an adjacent projection room and locks herself inside trapped she plays the tapes emily discovers the truth these are not aliens they are humans grotesquely mutated by longterm exposure to the planets atmosphere and an incurable virus that slowly erodes the brain causing aggression as it progresses the recordings reveal a secret program from world war three run by the director anas father which placed prisoners political enemies and expendable civilians on distant planets to test survivability the program was designed as a contingency plan for global collapse when earth was devastated by a nuclear strike and communication broke down the program was abandoned and eventually repurposed as the current program emily is working in the humans on these planets were left behind to die emily breaks she vomits collapses and sobs overwhelmed by the realization that the mission she believed in is built on atrocity suddenly ivan appears and forcibly pulls her from the building outside emily is silent barely responsive ivan finally begins to talk haltingly as if confessing something hes been carrying alone he explains that he tried to help the people here but failed the infection is incurable the most aggressive among them attacked him forcing him to amputate his own leg to survive he explains that when they landed he ivan wasnt obsessed about there being aliens but rather hellbent on exposing the truth about the atrocities committed here ana refused she claimed ignorance saying her father told her the program used volunteers who were safely returned but ultimately admitted she couldnt allow her fathers reputation to be destroyed oliver hesitated conflicted urging caution rather than action when a crisis arose near the ship ana made a choice she left ivan behind oliver resisted then gave in he talks about ana and oliver briefly however emily is shattered by this she insists they have to help the people on the planet no matter the cost ivan warns her its dangerous and likely futile but emily doesnt care anymore she returns to the building and promises the survivors that she will expose the truth ivan hesitates then follows meanwhile back on the ship ana and oliver appear again in brief tense scenes threaded through the act they are barely speaking oliver attempts distraction avoidance anything to keep from confronting what theyve done but it fails eventually ana focuses on the practical problem navigation using her experience as a pilot she discovers a way to reroute the ship using previously traveled pathways even without full control her first instinct is to leave to put as much distance between themselves and the planet as possible oliver stops her he argues not emotionally but simplythat leaving is worse worse than staying worse than facing ivan worse than facing emily ana doesnt respond at first eventually she changes course the ship redirects moving back toward the planet the act ends with the spaceship approaching the planet from orbit while on the surface emily and ivan begin forming a plan ivan remains hesitant and deeply afraid emily is resolute no longer concerned with her own safety only with the truth act five opens with a flashback from olivers point of view revealing what truly happened the day he ana and ivan first landed on the planet they find the humans and the humans tell them everything ivan wants to expose the company ana however is more hesitant the two argue and it results in ana leaving the planet with oliver actively choosing to leave ivan behind the focus is on olivers silence and complicity contextualising his guilt and setting the emotional tone for the act the story then cuts to the present ana and oliver land on the planet following emilys tracker oliver leads for the first time taking initiative while ana remains withdrawn and silent allowing him control he suggests they stay together no matter what ana quietly agrees though she knows its already too latetheir bond fractured the moment she abandoned ivan meanwhile emily and ivan locate the evacuation pod ivan confirms he can repair it though it will take time which allows them to properly gather evidence during this process emily finally realises that ivan is infected with the same degenerative virus affecting the planets human inhabitants details shed previously noticed but never connected ivan is resigned to it emily is not she insists they will find a cure once they return to earth ivan challenges her motivations asking why shes sacrificing everything for this emily answers that its the right thing to do but when pressed for something deeper she has no response they are interrupted by movement both freeze as ana and oliver emerge the four stand in silence emily is shocked and deeply hurt at the sight of ana though she masks it ivan is openly terrified oliver is hit with the full weight of guilt at how broken emily and ivan look ana feels it too though she cant articulate it oliver is the first to speak apologising directly to ivan when he steps forward ivan recoils ready to flee but emily stops him oliver backs away respecting the boundary emily then states plainly that she knows everything and intends to fix it ana attempts to say theyre there to help speaking in detached impersonal terms but emily shuts her down telling her shes done enough damage ivan suggests leaving altogether but emily instead decides that ana and oliver need to see the consequences she brings them back to the research facility inside ana and oliver confront the mutated humans and the evidence left behind both are visibly shaken ana admits she never knew the full extent of the program again and while emily believes her she makes it clear that ana still enabled the system that allowed it to happen emily shows them the tapes oliver breaks down finally realising that his silence was a choice and a wrong one he offers to help apologising through tears ana remains quiet emotionally shut down emily assigns oliver and ivan to organise and secure the logs while she records anas testimony she tells ivan theyll use the spaceship instead of the evacuation pod allowing them to transport both evidence and survivors still wary emily keeps copies of the logs herself as ivan and oliver work together they talk oliver apologises without asking for forgiveness ivan doesnt forgive him but he listens its not reconciliation but it is honesty emily confronts ana alone their conversation is raw and brutal ana initially lashes out defensively then collapses under the weight of it all finally admitting the atrocities she let happen some of the humans speak to her as well angry but clear that her father bears the greatest responsibility with the evidence secured emily announces theyre leaving using the ship oliver agrees immediately ana says nothing panic simmering beneath the surface ivan then reveals he is staying behind some of the humans will stay too he believes there is nothing left for him on earth and that the infection will kill him regardless emily argues desperately that a cure is possible ivan refuses quietly admitting that he no longer wants to be cured ana finally speaks trying to reach him ivan snaps back that thanks to her hes realised how disposable his life always was the moment is framed not as justice but as a deep injustice something said that cannot be taken back ana breaks desperate for control she declares they are not leaving she says she wants things to go back to how they were that she hates herself for destroying the only happiness shes ever known she threatens the logs but no one truly believes shell go through with it emily pulls ana aside into the log room and tells her to stopaccept that actions have consequences ana responds by turning the confrontation physical the two fight brutally emotionally without restraint emily overpowers ana pinning her down and choking her as ana repeats that she gives up that shell give them the ship emily doesnt stop until she remembers her coworker her parents the cycle of violence its shown here that emily may be the reason her father died her father was highly abusive and emily retliated against it by smashing a bottle on his head in self defense he left the house and never came back she thinks back on this moment and she releases ana emily takes what she needs and prepares to leave ana behind oliver intervenes hysterical but resolute insisting ana must come back as she is evidence herself reluctantly emily agrees they leave the planet with the logs survivors oliver ana and emily ivan stays behind in the aftermath the truth is exposed at first the public is split the company tries to cover everything up people dont believe it but then videos and photos are shown the director is arrested along with the companys leadership new scientific teams take over olivers sample becomes the foundation for restoring earths ecosystem a slow process but a real one oliver testifies accepting the fallout that comes with it he stays with the company to help with the sample ana testifies as well she is stripped of her titles reputation and power everything she built is gone emily reunites with her family and dedicates herself to rebuilding the earth developing machines that restore soil and ecosystems ten years later earth is visibly recovering emily thrives professionally though she carries a quiet heaviness after a day at work she unexpectedly runs into oliver they share coffee reminisce and speak of the past emily admits she doesnt know what became of ivan oliver hesitates then reveals that he only came to ask that she talk to ana who sits on her deathbed emily is upset at this at the fact that oliver and ana are still in contact but after some convincing she agrees to think on it oliver asks to remain in contact but emily doesnt answer emily visits ana a few days later they speak through a glass wall as anas disease is infectious they talk briefly awkwardly the exchange ends with emily saying she enjoyed their time together but she cannot have ana in her life again and emily leaves even while ana weakly asks her not to the story ends with emily at work she sees a sprouting plant in the soil she looks at it her expression neutral before smiling softly and turning away continuing her work after reading through all of that its pretty bad but i dont know its still worth a try to get feedback

dishonest reporter of the year awards 2025 the year 2025 is drawing to a close on the gregorian calendar which can only mean one thing its time once again for honestreportings dishonest reporter of the year awards our annual exercise in recognizing the journalists broadcasters and media institutions who have worked tirelessly to ensure the public is misinformed misled or emotionally manipulated in the most industrious ways possible unlike the hideously drawnout academy awardswhere one must endure hours of sanctimony about climate change and so on from people who flew in on private jetswe are not sadists we go straight for the jugular which brings us immediately to the main event so without further ado the winner of the dishonest reporter of the year 2025 award is the bbc this should surprise no one 2025 was the british broadcasting corporations annus horribilis though it is becoming difficult to remember when the annus was anything else barely a week passed this year without the beeb finding itself embroiled in some fresh scandal apology or hastilyadded clarification the rot set in early february saw the bbc forced to pull its documentary gaza how to survive a warzone after it emerged that the narratorthe emotional centerpiece of the filmwas the teenage son of a hamas minister and that his mother had been paid by the production company responsible for the program an unfortunate oversight one might say if one were feeling charitable then came the subtitling a closer review revealed that where gazan interviewees spoke of jews and pledged to fight jihad bbc editors thoughtfully translated this into the more palatable israelis and the soothingly vague resistance presumably on the grounds that british viewers might find murderous jewhatred and holy war a touch less sympathetic by may the bbcs radio 4 today programfamously setting the days agendahad set off another fire alarm un humanitarian chief tom fletcher was invited on air and promptly announced that 14000 babies could die in gaza within 48 hours he repeated it the presenter offered minimal pushback the implication that israel was about to carry out the mass killing of gazan babies hung heavily in the studio air the claim was of course absurd which is precisely why it ricocheted through bbc output for the next two days like a journalistic norovirus the line appeared in multiple bbc stories spreading to other international media outlets eventually after the damage was done the bbc quietly clarified and edited mission accomplished and still things worsened june brought apologies and internal learning exercises after the bbc failed to cut a live glastonbury broadcast of a poppunk duo gleefully chanting death death to the idf july delivered a leaked zoom call in which the bbcs ceo of news deborah turness earnestly explained that hamas military and political wings should be considered distinct entities a distinction familiar only to terrorist apologists and the bbc editorial board from august onwards the apologies blurred into one another then came november and the storm of storms a leaked internal dossier laid bare the scale of the bbcs bias not merely on israel but across its coverage as a whole confirming what critics had long argued that editorial distortion was not just a bug but a feature embedded in newsrooms from london to jerusalem the year concluded with the double resignation of turness and bbc director general tim davie an institutional bow on a year of spectacular selfinflicted damage and so with consistency creativity and a truly heroic disregard for accuracy the bbc has more than earned its prize congratulations primetime nonapology award christiane amanpour she has had to do it so many times now that one might reasonably expect christiane amanpour to have perfected the art of the televised apology you would think she might have learned how to deliver a sorry that sounds vaguely sincere how to align facial expression with script how to avoid looking as though she is being forced to read a hostage note written by her producer and displayed on the teleprompter with a gun trained on her just out of shot alas despite a long and distinguished career punctuated by periodic mandatory contrition amanpour still hasnt quite grasped the mechanics of public remorse particularly when israel is involved over the years she has been compelled to apologize for a series of unscripted analytical flourishes including her onair description of the murder of rabbi leo dees family as a ganglandstyle shootout in 2023 and her lapse into hamasadjacent terminology when she referred to the idf as the israeli occupation forces in 2024 practice it seems does not make perfect so when we tuned into amanpours cnn show when the last living israeli hostages were being exchanged for palestinian prisoners we knew instinctively that another apology was being queued up backstage the giveaway came when amanpour mused casuallythat israeli hostages were probably treated better than the average gazan owing to their value as hamas pawns and chips it was an arresting moment we rewound the clip then rewound it again surely not but yes that is what she said so we did what we do best called it out publicly lodged a formal complaint with cnn and then sat back to watch as the antiamanpour social media storm gathered speed all that remained was to wait for the ritual cleansing it arrived later that same evening there was regret there was talk of remarks being insensitive and wrong there was the familiar vocabulary of editorial damage what people dont understand about jungian analytical psychology and cognitive functions mbti does not analyze vibe or behavior one of the biggest misconceptions about mbti is that it analyzes vibe or behavior it never did and it never claimed to yes certain behaviors commonly show up within the same types but that is not what the theory is about mbti explains cognitive processing how information enters the mind how it is processed how it is stored and how it reflects back into the outer world when understood properly it is an extremely elegant framework although belief should never be based solely on source prestige it matters that this theory originates from carl jung one of the sharpest psychological minds of the modern era and the founder of analytical psychology his work was never meant to be caf talk parts of it were later abandoned not because they were inaccurate but because accurately analyzing another humans psyche at that depth requires a level of experiential and clinical precision that is genuinely difficult to achieve the fourletter type is only a shortcut a second misunderstanding arises when two individuals with radically different traits share the same mbti type this happens because there is far more than the fourletter code the fourletter code and 16personalities was only developed to act as a caf talk something fun pseudoscience and it stripped the original model from its accuracy and professional nature the 16 types were developed as a shortcut a usability layer placed on top of the original cognitivefunction theory when the four sides of the mind and consciousness dynamics are included the system does not describe 16 personalities at all it describes 64 base variants each behaving very differently from the others cognitive functions are a model this is the most important point cognitive functions are a model a model does not need to visually resemble reality to be valid it only needs to produce correct conclusions in electrical and mechanical engineering models are used constantly to analyze systems too complex to solve directly a car driving down a road subject to wind resistance surface friction speed bumps engine force and countless variables is nearly impossible to solve on paper asis instead it is modeled using equations originally designed for electrical circuits that is a mathematical model cognitive functions are no different it does not matter whether the brain literally contains functions in the way the model describes what matters is whether the logic works and it does that is why this framework is not pseudoscience or teenage astrology it is the most accurate cognitive personality model humans have produced so far cognitively controlled processes account for roughly 3040 of brain activity when combined with adjacent psychological models the explained range reaches 5060 of human psychology and personality an extraordinarily high number by any scientific standard the community confuses theory with outcomes another issue is the community itself many people approach these subjects not to understand them but to fill an internal emptiness they watch random youtubers they search for the fastest possible conclusion they stop reading early their statements are not always completely wrong but they are inaccurate yes types appear to follow stereotypes but those stereotypes do not come from the theory itself they emerge indirectly from how different cognitive processes interact with life experiences it is not a rule that a certain type must be depressed some types simply contain a higher demographic and contextual not intrinsic types are ranges on a gradient this logic already exists elsewhere people are categorized as male or female yet this is not a binary of 1 and 1 masculine and
